## Part A — Mitigation audit of prior-stage Major findings (residual gaps only)

I checked each prior Major against the document's full text to determine whether the document already covers the concern elsewhere. Verdict per finding: **RESIDUAL** (missed entirely), **PARTIAL** (mitigated in one place, residual remains), or **CLOSED**. No prior Major was found to be wrong. None is CLOSED.

**A1. RESIDUAL (Major) — Role→wizard registry still triplicates; contradicts the document's own "no second registry" property.**
Prior: Stage 5 zoom_out Finding 1. Affected scope: line 222, Stage 4 table lines 377–379.
Verified: `ROLE_WIZARD` exists at `app/(auth)/register.tsx:77–96` — a second, identical map. The document still says line 222 "No second registry", line 379 promotes **only** `login-as.tsx`'s `RESUBMIT_WIZARD` to `lib/roleWizards.ts`, and line 377 leaves `register.tsx` "wizard branch untouched" — even though line 220 shows the **new operator funnel itself routes through `register.tsx:77–81`**, making the inline map load-bearing for launch. As written, implementation ends with three copies of the same mapping. Simplicity rationale: the consolidation property is one `grep` away from false; migrating `register.tsx:77–81` onto the shared lib (or amending the claim) is a one-line doc edit.

**A2. RESIDUAL (Major) — Server read path still proposes a new typed getter instead of reusing the existing helper.**
Prior: Stage 5 zoom_out Finding 2. Affected scope: Stage 1 table line 343.
Verified: `isVerticalEnabled(key: string): Promise<boolean>` exists at `lib/platformConfig.ts:150` — fresh uncached read, absent-key/failure fallback to `false` (exactly the design's fail-closed posture). Line 343 still reads "add a typed getter for the flag"; no section mentions the existing helper. One-word doc fix ("reuse `isVerticalEnabled`").

**A3. RESIDUAL (Major) — Surviving-vertical launch proof and the `shop_types` seeding prerequisite remain unaddressed.**
Prior: Stage 5 zoom_out Finding 3, sharpened by Stage 7 Design Critic Finding 5. Affected scope: line 35, G5/G6, CUJs 1–5, Stage 6 line 399.
Stage 6 still device-verifies only CUJs 1, 2, 3, 5 — ambulance is the only surviving vertical with a CUJ; no shop-order or parcel-order journey exists in the CUJ set, and "shop_types" appears nowhere in the document (the hub's category tiles depend on it). Partial mitigation exists (G5/G6 intent statements, inventory #19 location ownership) but the acceptance proof — the thing that makes "the launch product works end-to-end" (line 35) more than an assertion — is missing, and the inherited seeding prerequisite (concepts_brief Major 17) has still never been disposed of by any ruling or by this document.

**A4. RESIDUAL (Major) — Drawer group header "Ride" survives the hide inventory and the copy-discipline enumeration.**
Prior: Stage 7 Design Critic Finding 1. Affected scope: inventory #10 (line 157), Component D (lines 236, 333).
Verified: `components/GlobalActionButtons.tsx:60–63` carry `group: "Ride"` — including the "Services Hub" item itself (line 60) — and line 98 `GROUP_ORDER_CUSTOMER = ["Ride", "Activity", "Account"]`. After gating the four ride items, the launch-state drawer renders a section literally titled "Ride" containing only "Services Hub": a visible ride reference on every screen, violating G7's own definition (line 49) and the Copy Truth Rule (line 37). The document's hard-coded-literal list (line 333) and Component D do not enumerate it anywhere. Not mitigated; needs one inventory/Component D extension.

**A5. PARTIAL (Major) — Fail-closed constant's post-re-enable consequence still unstated; the prior recommendation should be refined.**
Prior: Stage 7 Design Critic Finding 2. Affected scope: line 44 (G2), line 142.
Partial mitigation: line 142 does state the constant's deliberate stage-invariance ("no stage-conditional fallback"), which is the correct zoom-out call — a last-known-value cache would add staleness logic to the exact mechanism the design froze for its simplicity, so I **refine the prior recommendation**: adopt option (a) only (record the accepted consequence — after CUJ 4 re-enables ride, a transient boot-fetch failure yields a ride-hidden session until the next cold start — as one accepted-consequence sentence, mirroring the exemplary line 140 pattern). The residual is one sentence, not a design change.

**A6. RESIDUAL (Major) — The no-flicker guarantee has no specified barrier on the unauthenticated path.**
Prior: Stage 7 Design Critic Finding 3. Affected scope: line 142, Stage 1 line 345.
Verified: `app/index.tsx:167–176` is a fixed 1.5s `setTimeout` that fires `runAuthCheck()` without awaiting any network call; the redirect chain (:144–157) runs on the verify-token response. The document's guarantee "resolved in memory before the login screen renders (no post-mount fetch wait or flicker)" (line 142) is real only for the authenticated path (awaited verify-token response); on the no-session path, Stage 1's wording ("fires GET /api/app-config **in parallel** during the hold", line 345) makes a fetch-outlasting-the-hold race the default. Residual: specify the barrier (no-session redirect awaits the config read with a bounded timeout, fail-closed before routing) or withdraw the no-flicker guarantee and state the degraded behavior.

**A7. RESIDUAL (Major) — "G5" goal-number collision.**
Prior: Stage 6 comprehension Finding 1, Stage 7 Style M1. Affected scope: lines 180, 243, 350 vs line 47.
Line 180's gloss "(first store submission)" partially mitigates one occurrence; lines 243 ("before G5") and the Stage 2 heading (line 350, "irreversible after G5") remain unmitigated against the Goals definition of G5 (services hub home, line 47). Rename the milestone or re-point to G1.

**A8. RESIDUAL (Major) — `mode="operator"` is an unplanned prerequisite on an existing file.**
Prior: Stage 6 comprehension Finding 2. Affected scope: line 219, Stage 4 lines 375–376.
Verified: `app/(auth)/phone-entry.tsx` takes no props and has no `mode` (the only "mode" on the file is `resizeMode` at :151); role selection is internal `useState`. The Stage 4 `phone-entry` row (line 375) lists only the re-skin, flag-gated pills, and links — gaining the parameter is planned nowhere. Mitigation-adjacent fact found this pass: `owner_dispositions_2026-11-11.md:66` records the wrapper as an "engineering correction," but a ruling-file one-liner is not an implementation plan. Residual: add the `mode` parameter to the Stage 4 phone-entry row.

**A9. RESIDUAL (Major) — rider/(rider) naming inversion still undefined.**
Prior: Stage 6 comprehension Finding 3. Affected scope: lines 172, 169 vs 225.
The document still links `(main)/(rider)` to driver surfaces only implicitly (line 172 "driver-framed hamburger items"; line 169 grouping it with ride routes) while line 225 maps the `rider` DB role to the customer-facing "User" label. No definitional sentence exists. One sentence closes it.

**A10. RESIDUAL (Major) — Unanchored review-finding citation scheme.**
Prior: Stage 7 Structural Finding 1 / Style M4 (repeat of comprehension Finding 4). Affected scope: lines 157–170, 354, 377.
Still unmitigated: "review Blocker 4" (×5), "review finding 6" (×2), "review (codebase B-4)", "(B-5)", and "owner spec 3c" resolve only by cross-file inference; line 9's brace-glob names no file→numbering registry. This pass adds one data point: `owner_dispositions_2026-11-11.md:66` contains the engineering-corrections list that "owner spec 3c" most plausibly refers to — but no itemized "3c" exists in any file, so the pointer remains dangling. Convention fix stands.

**A11. RESIDUAL (Major, by convergence) — D-9 divergence still unrecorded in the authoritative file.**
Prior: Stage 5 Nit 4, Stage 7 Design Critic Finding 4, Stage 7 Structural Finding 2. Affected scope: lines 169, 172 vs `owner_dispositions_2026-11-11.md:64`.
Verified this pass: D-9 still prescribes layout-level guards at `(tabs)/home/index.tsx` and `(main)/(rider)/_layout.tsx`; the ruling file is unamended. Line 172 partially mitigates by giving the superset rationale functionally ("(which already wraps every `(main)` route…)") without ever naming D-9. I raise this from Stage 5's Nit to the Stage 7 Structural/Critic severity because three independent stages converged on it and the authoritative file remains silent: the mechanism question is settled engineering; what remains is the record — amend the ruling (owner re-affirmation of D-9-as-centralized) and add one sentence at inventory #22.

**A12. RESIDUAL (Major, wording-class) — Launch product still enumerated four ways, 4-vs-5.**
Prior: Stage 7 Style M2. Affected scope: lines 24, 35 vs 47, 73.
Lines 24/35 list four verticals; lines 47/73 list five tiles (adding "shop categories"). A charitable reading reconciles them (a tile, not a vertical), but the document never states the reconciliation, and case/order drift across the four lists stands. One canonical enumeration sentence.

## Part B — Intermediate-altitude re-run of the zoom-out vectors

**Root-problem focus — confirmed.** The design still attacks the root problem (first launch must not be ride-hailing) through the 23-row inventory, one runtime flag, and one atomic identity decision; the central `RideSurfaceGuard` (Option B) is the simpler superset of D-9's two named guards and keeps ride files untouched, which is what the gate set requires. No symptom-patching found.

**YAGNI / simplicity — confirmed, with one boundary checked.** The Non-Goals, Alternative G/I rejections, and never-cached/one-boolean posture hold at intermediate altitude. Boundary checked this pass: the central guard's ride-route set (line 174) is a manually-maintained denylist whose *future* additions have no automated gate — but line 170 verifies initial completeness against the nav-integrity RESOLVED list and line 174 assigns the maintenance rule; adding an automated completeness gate now would be the speculative machinery Alternative G already rejected. Adequately mitigated; not a finding.

**Reuse — confirmed, two residuals already carried (A1, A2).** All other reuse claims hold: the location helper reuses the ride home's geocoding path (line 362), the flag seeds through the existing platform-config seed script, verify-token is additive, `GET /api/app-config` follows the existing `[public]` convention, and Observability reuses `configAuditLog` (line 412). No new reinvention found.

**Premature optimizations — none.** No caching, queues, or speculative abstractions; the once-per-cold-boot session cache is the minimum. The public endpoint's one-static-boolean shape makes rate limiting unnecessary at launch (no enumeration value, no per-user data) — its absence is correct YAGNI, consistent with the NFR statement at line 410.

**Architectural dead-ends — none new.** Every re-point is flag-conditional (line 369), the wrapper/registry/dropdown are additive over existing machinery, and the dormant-mode contract (line 174) prevents Node surfaces from importing ride surfaces. The bundle-ID rebuild consequence (line 186) is a documented operational cost, not a dead end.

**New finding (Nit) — the stage-4 "flag-off build" verification requirement has no stated flag-off environment before stage 6.**
Severity: Nit. Affected scope: line 242 vs lines 142, 399–401; extends Stage 7 Design Critic Finding 10 (which covered the missing lane for shop/parcel suites — this is the auth lane's sequencing twin).
Rationale: line 242 requires auth suites "verified on the flag-off build" in the same commit as stage 4, but staging stays flag-**on** (mandatory stage-1 seed, line 142) until stage 6 flips it (line 399), the client has no override (no build-time flags, Non-Goal line 58; fail-closed constant line 142), and the auth lane is dual-state — updated flows must stay green on flag-on dev builds *and* pass on flag-off. The document should state where the flag-off run happens: either the flag-off execution is scheduled at stage 6 (with stage 4 verifying the updated flows as authored on flag-on), or a temporary staging flip via T1 is the stage-4 mechanism. One sentence in the test plan.

**Prior Nits — no status changes.** Referenced, not re-reported: `node://payment/…` acceptance literal (Critic F6), favicon wording (F7), "relocated" verb (F8/Style M3), rows 20–21 "gated AND mount-guarded" wording (comprehension F5), Q-numbering registry (N17), unstated `expo-router.origin` value and unmotivated stage-2-first ordering (comprehension N9), iOS splash disposition (Stage 5 Nit 5).

## Verdict

**No new Blockers, no new Majors from this lens.** The document's architecture survives the intermediate pass exactly as Stage 5 found it: zoom-out-compliant, unusually disciplined on YAGNI, and correctly centralized where the prior round's owner resolution (Option B) put the guard. The material result of this stage is the **residual ledger**: all twelve prior Majors (A1–A12) remain open in the current text — none was wrong, none is closed, two are partial (A5, A7), and the rest are unmitigated. Eleven of the twelve close with doc-level edits of one line to one sentence; A3 and A4 additionally require an acceptance-scope extension (surviving-vertical E2E proof + `shop_types` disposition) and an inventory extension (drawer "Ride" group header) respectively. One new Nit (B) on flag-off build sequencing. Every claim added in this report was verified against the working tree; the two recommendation refinements are: fail-closed consequence → record it, do not cache it (A5); "owner spec 3c" → likely the dispositions-file engineering-corrections list, still unresolvable as cited (A10).
